the presence of oestrogen in intact females protects against the adverse cardiovascular effects of a reduced nephrons early in life, however, this protection is lost with ageing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nephron endowment is important to maintain cardiovascular and renal health in ageing female sheep.
the impact of reduced nephron endowement on cardiovascular health is gender specific and that this impact is dependent on the presence or absence of ovarian hormones.
the presence of an intact female ovary protects from the impact of reduced nephron endowments on cardiovascular and renal health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of reduced nephron endowments is different in males and females and that the protection afforded to females in early life is lost with ageing.
a reduced nephron number is associated with increased cardiovascular and renal risk in females and males, however, the impact of reduced nephron endowments is more severe in males and OVX females.
the nephron number at birth may not be the only determinant for the development of hypertension and cardiovascular disease later in life.
